evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of ATP6V0C possibly underlies 16p13.3 deletions that cause microcephaly, seizures, and neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of loss of function constraint metrics, transcript-aware evaluation of the population variants, GeVIR scores, analysis of reported pathogenic point variants, detailed review of the known functions of gene products and their animal models showed that the haploinsufficiency of ATP6V0C likely underlies the phenotype of this condition.

nodes.description: Heterozygous germline variants in ATP6V0C, the c subunit of the V0 proton-translocating domain of the V-ATPase. Two routes to reduced function are proposed. Truncating, stop-loss and whole-gene-deletion alleles act through haploinsufficiency, supported by halved transcript levels in a stop-loss carrier. Missense variants facing the a subunit are modelled as jamming the rotary mechanism and are proposed to act dominant-negatively; that second route is inferred from structure, not measured. The synaptic-vesicle-cycle step affected is neurotransmitter loading.

nodes.description: Expressing selected patient missense variants in worms reduces growth, worsens motor function and shortens lifespan, consistent with a deleterious effect of the missense alleles.

Pan-neuronal RNAi knockdown of the ATP6V0C orthologue prolongs recovery from electroshock-induced seizure-like behaviour in larvae. Levetiracetam and topiramate reverse it most strongly; phenytoin does not.

Fever sensitivity is common. In familial cases febrile seizures begin at 7 to 8 months, and fever-sensitive epilepsy is one of the more frequent presentations in which ATP6V0C variants are found. No cohort fraction is reported, so frequency is left unset.

nodes.description: The synaptic-vesicle-cycle step specific to this disorder. The proton electrochemical gradient generated by the vesicular V-ATPase drives the vesicular transporters that fill vesicles with neurotransmitter, so a reduced gradient is expected to underfill vesicles. The synaptic_vesicle_cycle module has no loading node; its protein deficiency node, which names neurotransmitter loading in its scope, is matched by the variant node above.

nodes.description: A proposed second route. The membrane V0 sector of the V-ATPase interacts with the SNARE machinery and the c subunit binds VAMP2; acute light inactivation of the c subunit in hippocampal neurons rapidly inhibits transmission. The V0 fusion role is debated, and no study has tested it for ATP6V0C patient variants.
